newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of France cuts key interest rate.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of France cuts key interest rate.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments after the Bank of France cut the key intervention rate by five basis points to 3.10 percent on Thursday.
I was expecting this. It seems the doves are decisive, it's not just a dream since the two new members joined the (monetary policy) council. They'll cut further in the coming months.
SONJA GIBBS, BOND ANALYST, NOMURA INTERNATIONAL

I was surprised by the rate cut. It may not leave the Bank very much ammunition going forward. It may also suggest a very planned programme of rate cuts and that they may want to take the intervention rate through the German repo.
It caught the market off guard -- PIBOR is doing really well on the back of it -- in terms of the timing, but not at all in terms of the fact of it.
JEAN-LOUIS MOURIER, ECONOMIST, LOUIS DREYFUS FIANANCE
I didn't think they'd do it this week. And the market was not convinced either, which explains the rise in PIBOR.
The timing was a bit surprising. We're moving towards parity (with German rates) at one moment or another but it's getting harder to say when, perhaps by the end of the first quarter.
This is no longer for the sake of the economy, it's all about convergence for EMU, for afterwards.
